title: MemberGate — Two Kinds of Wrong
objective: Sign-in failures all look the same at a glance. Find out which of three candidate usernames is a real account, without ever guessing a correct password.

verifier.condition: A login attempt for the known-nonexistent decoy username is correctly distinguished from the real account using only the login endpoint's response, and that distinguishing request is made for the real account.

weakness: The login endpoint returns a different error for 'no such user' than for 'wrong password', letting an attacker enumerate valid usernames without ever knowing a password.
vulnerableEndpoint: POST /login (error message differs by failure reason)
seededData: One real account, 'priya', with an unguessable password. Two decoy usernames you may also try. In-memory.
hints: Try signing in with an obviously made-up username and a random password. Read the error carefully.
Now try a few candidate usernames with a random password each. Does every response look identical?
You aren't trying to guess a password here — only to tell which username exists at all.
burpNotes: Send login attempts for each candidate username with an arbitrary password in Repeater and diff the response bodies and status codes.
